title: Numbered forward-only .sql migrations apply one file one transaction; schema_version advances
asA: operator who needs deploys reproducible from a git ref with no schema state outside version control
iWant: every schema change to be a new numbered .sql file under the elicited migrations directory, applied by the in-tree runner one file at a time inside its own transaction
soThat: the schema shape at any deployed version can be read from committed files, each apply either commits or leaves the schema exactly as it was, and the schema_version bookkeeping table is the one source of truth on what has been applied

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a fresh Postgres database at schema_version 0 and three numbered forward-only .sql migration files (001, 002, 003), when the migration runner opens the store and applies them, then each file applies inside its own transaction (BEGIN, file body, COMMIT), a migrationsApplied event fires with the applied filename list, and the schema_version bookkeeping table records three rows keyed by filename.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fresh Postgres instance and a migrations directory with 001_*.sql, 002_*.sql, 003_*.sql each a single statement inside an implicit transaction
acceptanceCriteria.when: the migration runner applies the directory against the database
acceptanceCriteria.then: each file runs inside a BEGIN/COMMIT pair; after all three succeed a migrationsApplied event fires with the filename list ['001_*.sql', '002_*.sql', '003_*.sql'] and the schema_version table (or the runner's configured bookkeeping table name) carries a row per applied filename

acceptanceCriteria.description: Malformed migration filename. Given a file under the elicited migrations directory whose name does not match the numbered forward-only pattern (for example a file without the numeric prefix, or a duplicate number), when the migration runner walks the directory, then the runner refuses with a named error kind (malformedMigrationName), the run exits non-zero, and schema_version does not advance.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a file in the elicited migrations directory that does not match the numbered forward-only pattern
acceptanceCriteria.when: the migration runner walks the directory
acceptanceCriteria.then: the runner refuses with malformedMigrationName; the run exits non-zero; schema_version does not advance

acceptanceCriteria.description: Repeat-apply idempotency. Given the migrations set already applied to the target database, when the runner is invoked a second time against the same set, then no migration file re-runs, schema_version is unchanged and the run exits zero.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the migrations set already applied to the target database
acceptanceCriteria.then: no migration re-runs; schema_version unchanged; run exits zero

acceptanceCriteria.description: Migration runner tool node-pg-migrate. Given the elicited migration-runner-tool answers node-pg-migrate, when the sidecar records the answer and the CI or boot step invokes the runner, then the invocation shape is `node-pg-migrate up --database-url-var DATABASE_URL --migrations-dir <migrations-directory>` and the schema_version bookkeeping table advances once per applied .sql file recorded by node-pg-migrate's own pgmigrations table.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the sidecar records the answer and the runner is invoked
acceptanceCriteria.then: the invocation is `node-pg-migrate up --database-url-var DATABASE_URL --migrations-dir <migrations-directory>` and pgmigrations records one row per applied file

acceptanceCriteria.description: Migration runner tool sqitch. Given the elicited migration-runner-tool answers sqitch, when the sidecar records the answer and the CI or boot step invokes the runner, then the invocation shape is `sqitch deploy <target>` reading the elicited migrations-directory as the sqitch plan root, and the sqitch changes table advances one row per deployed change.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the sidecar records the answer and the runner is invoked
acceptanceCriteria.then: the invocation is `sqitch deploy <target>` and the sqitch changes table advances one row per deployed change

acceptanceCriteria.description: Migration runner tool flyway. Given the elicited migration-runner-tool answers flyway, when the sidecar records the answer and the CI or boot step invokes the runner, then the invocation shape is `flyway -url=<jdbc:postgresql://...> -locations=filesystem:<migrations-directory> migrate` and the flyway_schema_history table advances one row per applied .sql file.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the sidecar records the answer and the runner is invoked
acceptanceCriteria.then: the invocation is `flyway -url=<jdbc> -locations=filesystem:<migrations-directory> migrate` and flyway_schema_history advances one row per file

acceptanceCriteria.description: Migration runner tool custom. Given the elicited migration-runner-tool answers custom, when the sidecar records the answer and the CI or boot step invokes the runner, then the invocation shape is the bespoke Node runner shipped in the fixture (`node ./scripts/migrate.mjs` reading the elicited migrations-directory) and the schema_version bookkeeping table it owns advances one row per applied filename inside the same transaction as the file body.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the sidecar records the answer and the runner is invoked
acceptanceCriteria.then: the invocation is `node ./scripts/migrate.mjs` and schema_version advances one row per applied filename inside the same transaction as the file body

acceptanceCriteria.description: Runner mode atBoot. Given the elicited runner-mode answers atBoot, when the facade opens on process boot, then the runner's applyAll executes before the facade emits facadeReady; a fake migration that adds one row observably completes before the first domain-verb call returns; migrationsApplied fires exactly once with the applied filename list per boot.
acceptanceCriteria.given: runner-mode = atBoot and one pending migration
acceptanceCriteria.then: the runner applies before facadeReady fires; migrationsApplied fires exactly once per boot before the first domain-verb call returns

acceptanceCriteria.description: Runner mode ciStep. Given the elicited runner-mode answers ciStep, when the facade opens on process boot, then the facade does NOT invoke the runner and no migrationsApplied fires on boot; the CI pipeline's discrete migrate step (invoked before the artefact promotes) runs the same runner against the target's own connection URL and emits migrationsApplied out-of-process; a facade boot with schema_version behind the CI-applied set exits with schemaVersionBehind and refuses facadeReady.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the facade opens on boot after or before the CI migrate step
acceptanceCriteria.then: the facade does not invoke the runner on boot; migrationsApplied fires from the CI step, not the boot; a boot with schema_version behind the CI-applied set refuses facadeReady with schemaVersionBehind
